D.t: Hallie Shoffner trails by 11.6 and wins 3% of simulations. Closing it takes about 56,984 voters switching sides, or 113,968 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +19.0 and R +4.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +9.7. Your best recent poll is GrayHouse (R) at R +8.6; your worst is Hendrix College at R +10.4. 2 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Pulaski, a projected net 59,293 votes; Washington, a projected net 13,774 votes; Jefferson, a projected net 8,377 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Benton, R +11.7, 10.3% of the vote; Mississippi, R +6.4, 0.9% of the vote; Ouachita, D +1.6, 0.7% of the vote; Clark, D +3.4, 0.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Hallie Shoffner runs furthest behind in Miller, Baxter, Boone. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 83% of voters, 36 to 59, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.15 points; Voters without a degree, 68% of voters, 40 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.40 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 65% of voters, 40 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.27 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Hallie Shoffner: Immigration voters 18 to 78, Small counties 32 to 64, Incomes $125K and up 34 to 62. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.4M cash against $6.8M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
